summary: Partial research checkpoint: declaration-sized polynomial node algebra plus flat ambient ideal/dual/quotient transport and actual noetherian module-completion comparisons. The Appendix relative stable-reflexivity criterion and its unproved/cited completion inputs are recorded precisely, not certified by these ambient adapters. All stages and the shared key remain partial; every implementation status is unchecked. This continuation gives the canonical coefficient-linear section splitting and replaces private evaluation division by the built two-variable kernel criterion. This checkpoint instantiates the canonical coefficient splitting on the native ideal: six granular coefficient-action, evaluation-linearity, projection and promoted projection-law nodes, three projection APIs and four boundary tests; an immutable admission-free proof extraction verifies the canonical bodies separately from the admitted submitted sketch.

nodes.title: Moduli stacks of pointed curves
nodes.statement: Define a single moduli pseudofunctor CurvesModuli(ε,g,n), ε=smooth or stable, on schemes. Its fibre over S is the groupoid of parent curve families f:C→S, proper flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of arithmetic genus g and an ordered list of n disjoint sections through the relative smooth locus. In the stable flavour fibres are nodal and ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) is relatively ample; the smooth flavour is the full subcategory with f smooth. Arrows are marking-preserving S-isomorphisms; pullback is scheme-theoretic base change with its canonical associator. Write M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n}. This is a groupoid-valued functor; no coarse or fine representability is built into its definition.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the parent’s stable-pointed and smooth-curve family data, without redefining stability.
Form the fibre groupoid using marking-preserving relative isomorphisms.
Use pullback universal properties to obtain coherent reindexing; the effective-descent assertion is a separate node.
acceptance: The genus-zero stable range begins at n=3; a two-pointed rational curve is excluded.
A self-node contributes two normalization flags to stability.

sources.match: The cited passage supplies the construction or proof in the stated range; qualifications and upstream inputs are explicit in the statement and prerequisites.

api.name: CurvesModuli.obj
api.statement: The fibre groupoid over S has precisely the parent smooth/stable pointed families as objects.

api.name: CurvesModuli.iso
api.statement: Morphisms are exactly S-isomorphisms carrying every ordered marking to the marking of the same index.

api.name: CurvesModuli.pullback
api.statement: For T→S pull back the family and every section; identity and composition agree via coherent canonical isomorphisms.

api.name: CurvesModuli.smoothInclusion
api.statement: The smooth flavour is the full subcategory of the stable flavour on smooth families.

api.name: CurvesModuli.geometricPoints
api.statement: Over an algebraically closed field the objects and automorphism groups are those of pointed curves, not only isomorphism classes.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.rationalThree
tests.statement: Over an algebraically closed field the smooth three-pointed rational curve has a unique isomorphism to (P¹;0,1,∞) and trivial automorphism group.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.rationalTwoExcluded
tests.statement: (P¹;0,∞) fails the stable-range condition and has a positive-dimensional automorphism group.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.ellipticInvolution
tests.statement: In characteristic zero a pointed elliptic curve (E,0) has the nontrivial automorphism [−1]; its fibre groupoid is not a discrete set.

tests.name: CurvesModuli.selfNodeFlags
tests.statement: An irreducible rational nodal curve with one smooth marking is stable of arithmetic genus one: the normalization has three special flags.

uses.how: One shared definition for smooth and stable pointed families, their automorphisms and classifying maps.

nodes.title: Monic normal form in the section ring
nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). For every r∈R there is a unique pair (p,q₁)∈A[Y]² with r=p(v)+u q₁(v). Thus R is free over A[Y] with basis (1,u), and free over A by the monomials vⁿ,u vⁿ.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: Use the pinned AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' supplied by monic remainder division. Over nontrivial A, natDegree_quadratic identifies its dimension as two.
Reindex that basis by Fin 2. Its vectors are 1 and u; basis reconstruction supplies p(v)+u q₁(v), and applying the basis representation to an equality proves uniqueness of both coefficients.
Over the zero ring, Module.subsingleton makes both the quotient and the pair of coefficient polynomials subsingleton, proving the same unique-existence statement.
Monic.free_adjoinRoot gives freeness over A[Y]. Compose its power basis with Polynomial.basisMonomials using Basis.smulTower to obtain freeness over A; no truncation of v is introduced.
acceptance: No relation truncating powers of v is introduced.

hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: In the unique two-coefficient form, multiplication by d multiplies each coefficient polynomial by Y−t.

The native proof uses freeness over A[Y] to obtain Module.IsTorsionFree; apply IsRegular.isSMulRegular to the monic polynomial Y−t, then identify this scalar multiplication with multiplication by v−ιt. nodes.title: Kernel of section evaluation
nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). ev∘ι=id_A, ker(ev)=J, and 0→J→R→A→0 splits A-linearly by ι.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: Use the built AdjoinRoot.induction_on to represent r by a bivariate polynomial P. The built lift_mk and eval₂_evalRingHom identify section evaluation with (P.eval(C s)).eval t.

The built Polynomial.mem_span_C_X_sub_C_X_sub_C_iff_eval_eval_eq_zero puts every vanishing representative in span{C(Y−t),X−C(s)}. This already proves the two-variable division statement; do not plan a private generic remainder lemma.
Map that ideal through the actual AdjoinRoot.mk using Ideal.mem_map_of_mem and Ideal.map_span. Its two generator images are v−ιt and u−ιs, so the image lies in J.
Conversely both generators evaluate to zero. Ideal.span_le puts J in the actual evaluation kernel. AdjoinRoot.lift_of and evaluation on constants give ev∘ι=id_A.

The A-linear splitting is made explicit by the separate section-evaluation-split construction. This proof does not use a normal-form basis, noetherianity, a unit discriminant or flatness of a coefficient map.
acceptance: The splitting is A-linear; the section map ι is not R-linear for the evaluation action on A.

nodes.title: Coefficient-linear splitting of section evaluation
nodes.statement: For the actual polynomial node ring R and J=ker(ev), construct the canonical A-linear equivalence e:R≃J×A, e(r)=(r−ι(ev(r)),ev(r)); its inverse sends (j,a) to j+ι(a). This makes 0→J→R→A→0 split over A, including the zero base ring, and fixes the maps rather than only an abstract isomorphism class.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: Use the existing inherited A-module structures on R, J and A; coefficient-inclusion-action identifies the actual coefficient inclusion with the native algebra map.
Define e(r)=(p(r),ev(r)), with p the actual section-evaluation-projection, and inverse (j,a)↦j+ι(a).
The forward/inverse identities follow from p(j)=j, p(ι(a))=0 and ev(j)=0. The other composition is the additive identity r−ιev(r)+ιev(r)=r.

Use p’s LinearMap laws and section-evaluation-scalars for addition and scalar multiplication. This directly instantiates the canonical formulas without an uninstantiated complementary-submodule adapter.
The inherited zero-base, nonreduced and non-R-linear tests all check against these actual bodies. No chosen basis or inverse discriminant is used.
acceptance: The equivalence is over A, with the actual ideal carrier J and actual evaluation map; never strengthen it to an R-linear splitting.
No finite A-rank or R-flatness of J is implied.

nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). With the characterized ε, every h∈D has a unique expression h=r·incl+ια·ε with (r,α)∈R×A.

Write z=ι(ev z)+cx+dy and use cε=−a incl, dε=b incl.

hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Induct from the unpointed stack using the universal-curve equivalence.
In the local universal nodal chart xy=t replace the base parameter t by xy; the total chart remains smooth and the boundary becomes a product of coordinates.
Properness and the DM property are preserved by the representable proper universal curve.
acceptance: This induction does not assume the genus-one base.

nodes.title: The rigid triangle locus
nodes.statement: Attach to a one-pointed genus-one curve the rigid three-component rational triangle carrying the two ordered extra markings of Knudsen’s construction. The resulting genus-two two-pointed family identifies M̄₁,₁ with the specified closed intersection of three boundary branches in M̄₂,₂; the labelled rational subcurve is uniquely recoverable.

proofSteps: Use the parent family gluing and stable-flag criterion for the rigid labelled rational subcurve.
Recover the genus-one component and attachment section from the distinguished labelled triangle; check the comparison on families and isomorphisms.
The local nodal chart cuts out the three triangle smoothing coordinates. A nodal genus-one component supplies a fourth boundary parameter.
acceptance: This is the specific rigid locus, not a claim that every separating clutching is a closed immersion.

Attach the rigid labelled rational triangle to the pointed genus-one curve to obtain the specified closed substack of M̄₂,₂.

nodes.title: Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen theorem
nodes.statement: For every stable pair (g,n), M̄_{g,n} is a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Z of relative dimension3g−3+n. The smooth substack M_{g,n} is open dense and its complement has relative normal crossings.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Induct on n using the universal-curve equivalence.
In a nodal chart replace the old smoothing coordinate t by uv; the total chart is smooth over Z and the boundary equation replaces t by the product uv.
Start separately at (0,3),(1,1), and (g,0) for g≥2. Properness and the DM diagonal pass through the representable universal curve.
acceptance: The relative dimension is0 at (0,3) and1 at both (0,4) and (1,1).

nodes.title: Separating clutching morphism
nodes.statement: For ordered complementary marking sets I,J and g₁+g₂=g, with stable source pairs (g₁,|I|+1),(g₂,|J|+1), define ξ_{g₁,I}:M̄_{g₁,I∪{a}}×M̄_{g₂,J∪{b}}→M̄_{g,n} by gluing a and b in the disjoint union. The new node is distinguished in the construction, but is forgotten in the target. The two source components may each already be reducible.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Apply the parent’s external scheme clutching and reindex the remaining markings.
Its arbitrary-base-change and isomorphism compatibility define the stack morphism.

uses.how: Both clutching morphisms are representable finite and unramified. For a fixed target stable curve their geometric fibres are finite choices of a node and, when relevant, an ordering or genus/marking assignment to its branches. These choices can be more than one even for a fixed separating genus and marking partition.

A pointed boundary type is a stable connected genus-g graph with n labelled legs and exactly one edge, up to label-preserving graph isomorphism, using the parent’s weighted dual graphs. Its normalization parameter stack is the product of the vertex moduli stacks modulo the finite automorphism group of this graph. For n=0,g≥2 the types are Δ₀ and Δᵢ for1≤i≤⌊g/2⌋, where Δ₀ is the closure of the nonseparating one-node locus, not merely the locus of irreducible nodal curves.
Under separating clutching, ξ*E_g≅pr₁*E_{g₁}⊕pr₂*E_{g₂}, hence ξ*λ_g≅pr₁*λ_{g₁}⊗pr₂*λ_{g₂}. The isomorphism is equivariant for permitted graph exchanges using the determinant convention.

nodes.title: Nonseparating clutching morphism

proofSteps: Apply the parent’s self-clutching pushout with its base-change isomorphisms.
Use the parent graph-genus formula to obtain genus g.
acceptance: An unlabelled nonseparating node does not order its branches.

Its finite map to the boundary records a distinguished node; it separates branches at curves with several nodes of the same type.

For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} and retained i, let D_{i,n+1} be the divisor of a rational tail carrying exactly marks i,n+1 and its attachment. Then Lᵢ on the source is π*Lᵢ⊗O(D_{i,n+1}); equivalently π*Lᵢ=Lᵢ⊗O(−D_{i,n+1}).

For g≥2 let Δ be the effective Cartier divisor M̄_g minus M_g, with coefficient1 on each reduced local node branch. Its global decomposition is Δ=Σ_{i=0}^{⌊g/2⌋}Δᵢ according to the one-edge unpointed types. For a generically smooth stable family over an integral noetherian S, its pullback is an effective Cartier divisor Δ_S; arbitrary families mapping entirely into Δ do not have this effective-Cartier pullback.

nodes.title: Coarse spaces of pointed curve stacks
nodes.statement: For each stable pair construct the coarse algebraic spaces q:M̄_{g,n}→M̄^{coarse}_{g,n} and q°:M_{g,n}→M^{coarse}_{g,n}. They are initial for maps to algebraic spaces and induce bijections between geometric points and isomorphism classes. Stable coarse spaces are proper over Z. Existence alone gives neither smoothness of the coarse space nor a universal family on it; base change is used only with the hypotheses of the imported coarse-space theorem.

For g≥2 M̄^{coarse}_g is a projective scheme over Z. There is a positive power of a sufficiently high pluricanonical determinant which descends to an ample line on the coarse algebraic space.

The fixed symplectic component M_g[N] over Z[1/N,ζ_N] is a smooth quasi-projective scheme of relative dimension3g−3, carrying a smooth projective universal curve of genus g. Forgetting level to M_g is representable finite étale. It is regular; geometric irreducibility is the separate connectedness theorem.

For an integral finite-type base S over a field and a smooth genus-g family, g≥2, maximal variation means that the coarse classifying map S→M_g^{coarse} is generically quasi-finite onto its image. The definition uses geometric curve isomorphism classes, not choices of frames or markings.

Over an algebraically closed field k, the coarse stable curve moduli admits a morphism t̄:M̄_g^{coarse}→A_g^{min} extending smooth Torelli. On a stable curve it uses the abelian part of the generalized Jacobian and maps to the corresponding minimal-compactification stratum. The descended rational Hodge line satisfies λ_coarse=t̄*ω_min, with ω_min ample.

nodes.title: Full symplectic level on smooth curves
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2 and N≥3 invertible on the base. A full Jacobi level structure on a smooth genus-g curve is an isomorphism α:(Z/N)^{2g}→J(C)[N] carrying the standard alternating form to the Weil pairing through a chosen trivialization of μ_N, or equivalently a homogeneous symplectic-similitude identification without choosing that trivialization. Use the fixed symplectic flavour over Z[1/N,ζ_N], and the similitude flavour over Z[1/N]. Their components and universal families are not identified without this choice.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the relative Jacobian of the smooth curve family, its principal polarization and prime-to-characteristic torsion pairing; the curve-relative representability input is a recorded extension gap.
Define the isomorphism functor with its exact pairing condition and marking-preserving curve isomorphisms.
acceptance: N is invertible; level at the characteristic is a different problem.

uses.how: For a smooth genus-g curve g≥2 over an algebraically closed field with N≥3 prime to the characteristic, an automorphism acting trivially on full N-torsion of its Jacobian is the identity. Consequently the curve full-level stack has trivial inertia.

The fixed symplectic component M_g[N] over Z[1/N,ζ_N] is a smooth quasi-projective scheme of relative dimension3g−3, carrying a smooth projective universal curve of genus g. Forgetting level to M_g is representable finite étale. It is regular; geometric irreducibility is the separate connectedness theorem.

Over the fixed pairing base and for g≥2, form τ:M_g[N]→A_g[N] by the relative Jacobian with its canonical principal polarization and induced full level. The pullback of the universal abelian scheme is canonically Jac(C_g/M_g[N]); in particular the square of abelian schemes is Cartesian.

nodes.title: Connectedness of a pairing component
nodes.statement: Every geometric fibre of the full Jacobi-level scheme over Spec Z[1/N,ζ_N] is connected, hence irreducible by smoothness. The homogeneous-similitude scheme over Z[1/N] is not asserted geometrically connected without fixing the multiplier.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.

nodes.title: Torsion freeness of the stable-stack Picard group
nodes.statement: For g≥2 Pic(M̄_{g,C}) is torsion free. A torsion line gives a finite cyclic cover of the stack. Over Teichmüller space this cover splits; its character factors through the mapping-class group, and extending over every boundary kills each Dehn-twist generator, so the cover and line are trivial.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: The proof uses connected simply connected Teichmüller space, the analytic presentation of the smooth stack and generation by Dehn twists. These general analytic inputs have no verified atlas supplier and are recorded as gaps.
Use the one-node smoothing monodromy to identify the boundary loop with the corresponding Dehn twist.
Since the cover extends over that divisor, its cyclic monodromy on the loop vanishes; all generators vanish.
acceptance: Retain stack stabilizers; passing first to the coarse space is not this proof.

hypotheses: All coefficient rings are commutative and may have zero divisors or be the zero ring. No noetherianity, unit discriminant, injectivity or flatness of f is required. Statements concern the explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.
proofSteps: The displayed product is additive and A-balanced separately in both pairs, using the coefficient scalar tower on D; extend it by the tensor universal property.

nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. Construct the canonical A′-linear equivalence E_{Q,f}:A′⊗_A Q≃Q′ satisfying E_{Q,f}(a′⊗[h])=[E_D(a′⊗h)] and E_Q′(E_{Q,f}(a′⊗z))=a′f(E_Q(z)). sourceIssues.reason: Over C glue three pairwise nonisomorphic elliptic curves in a chain and put the sole mark on the central curve. The genus3 target has two distinct nodes of type (1,empty)|(2,{1}). Choosing the left or right elliptic tail gives nonisomorphic geometric preimages in M̄₁,₁×M̄₂,₂, since the first elliptic factors are nonisomorphic. A closed immersion is injective on geometric points. This is a statement counterexample, distinct from Ile’s correction to the proof of3.7.
